nodes.description: Impaired endothelial adhesion and barrier function in the lymphatic endothelium yields malformed, incompetent and leaky lymphatic vessels. In an affected child, lymphoscintigraphy and MR lymphangiography showed abnormal lymphatic flow with dermal backflow, abdominal and pedal lymphatic leakage, and narrowing of the thoracoabdominal thoracic duct. The lymphatic-endothelial-specific mechanism of THSD1 has not been directly demonstrated; it is inferred from the general endothelial barrier role and from the human lymphatic phenotype.

nodes.description: THSD1 maintains the endothelial barrier by activating FAK-PI3K signaling that drives Rac1-mediated actin cytoskeletal regulation of adherens junctions and focal adhesion assembly, and by suppressing autophagy-mediated turnover of adhesions. Loss of THSD1 destabilizes endothelial cell attachment and barrier integrity. The mechanism was defined in blood-vascular endothelium — Thsd1 knockdown causes severe hemorrhage in zebrafish embryos and the mouse retina, and the FAK-PI3K/Rac1 axis was shown in cultured human endothelial cells — and is extrapolated to the lymphatic endothelium whose failure produces the human phenotype.
nodes.id: Impaired Endothelial Focal Adhesion and Barrier Integrity

evidence.reference_title: THSD1 preserves vascular integrity and protects against intraplaque haemorrhaging in ApoE-/- mice.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistic studies in human endothelial cells demonstrated that THSD1 activates FAK-PI3K, leading to Rac1-mediated actin cytoskeleton regulation of adherens junctions and focal adhesion assembly.

evidence.reference_title: THSD1 preserves vascular integrity and protects against intraplaque haemorrhaging in ApoE-/- mice.

evidence.reference_title: THSD1 Is a Multifaceted Regulator in Health and Disease.
evidence.snippet: THSD1 promotes focal adhesion assembly and suppresses autophagy-mediated adhesion turnover, thereby stabilizing endothelial attachment and maintaining barrier function.

evidence.reference_title: THSD1 Suppresses Autophagy-Mediated Focal Adhesion Turnover by Modulating the FAK-Beclin 1 Pathway.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, THSD1 negatively regulates Beclin 1, a central autophagy regulator, at FAs through interactions with focal adhesion kinase (FAK). THSD1 inactivation diminishes FAK activity and relieves its inhibitory phosphorylation on Beclin 1.

nodes.description: THSD1 encodes a transmembrane cell-surface protein bearing a thrombospondin type 1 domain, originally identified as a marker of hematopoietic and endothelial cells. Biallelic truncating (frameshift/nonsense) variants remove structural and functional domains and abolish THSD1 function. The recurrent human allele is a homozygous eight-nucleotide deletion (p.Arg388Glnfs*66) that produces a severely truncated protein.
